title: Working full time while doing a master's abroad
end_why: after her last word ("…and not to die. Yeah."); the rest is room tone
summary: She talks almost without pauses (no gap over 1.2 s inside her speech, apart from one inside a retake), so the gain comes from 6 retakes and stumbles plus the end. She starts speaking at 0.07 s, so there is no dead air at the start.

cuts.why: She stops mid-phrase ("doing a full time-"), adds an aside, then says the phrase again. Keeping the second take gives "I'm also doing a full-time master's degree here as well". If she likes the aside "I like to add full time to it", skip this cut.
Restart: first take breaks off ("gets scratched up"), second take is clean: "before the semester gets busy".
"one of the tip, tip, tip is to block, block": keeps "if you have a full-time job, block your week, right?"
Same sentence twice; the second ("A good way to plan your week is to start with the things that cannot move") is the complete one.
She corrects herself ("20, 30 calendar days, I think …"); keeps the corrected take "30 calendar days of study leave. And 20 of those are paid".

An "um" and three goes at the same line ("So I can work around the clock as well. I don't know. Yeah, I can work around the clock."); keeps the last, firm one: "I work around the clock. But depending on the job…"

decisions:
- **Cut 1 of section 2** (the "I like to add full time to it" aside at 0:05) is optional: it's a personal touch, but it breaks the first sentence of the video.
- **9:43 "Try to, I don't know, this advice is the one for me as well, but try to, you know, get proper sleep"**: left in (it sounds like her), but it is a loose sentence; optional cut 9:41.90 (581.90) to 9:46.58 (586.58) so it reads "…at least get sleep. You know, get proper sleep. It helps." (not counted in the totals)
- **Ending**: the video ends on "…stay on top of things and not to die. Yeah." with no sign-off. Her kit had a closing line ("tell me in the comments which of these tips you already do") that she did not record.
- Unclear words to listen to: 1:19 "Working while studying is the real ghetto(?)", 5:49 "you can … at your work", 6:13 "School will take a lot of my blood(?) in December", 7:53 "affords you some strap(?) privileges", 9:14 "You cannot be cooking a four-year-old(?) on Wednesday afternoon" (whisper's words; meaning unclear, probably a Nigerian dish).
kit:
**Skipped from the kit** (she didn't say these):
- The 1994 planning-fallacy study (Roger Buehler, Dale Griffin, Michael Ross: students guessed 34 days for their thesis, took about 55, about 30% finished on time). She gave the advice ("budget 10 weeks if you think 6-8") without the study.
- Cal Newport's name for time blocking (she says "It's called time blocking").
- The 2019 MIT sleep study (88 chemistry students) and the Mike and Matty "bedtime, not alarm" rule.
- Tip 7 "be honest with yourself about what you have / don't hold on to a picture of a perfect work-life balance / be willing to give things up" (partly said in her own words at the end).
- "Tell your manager in advance: I have this big thing at school and I want to take study leave."
- The detail about her big practical course with real clients (she says instead she'll be rounding off courses, doing presentations, cleaning up projects in December).
- The closing call to action ("tell me in the comments which of these tips you already do").
- Tip numbers stop after six: from vacation days on she says "another thing" / "another tip" (communication, kind of job, meal prep, sleep).

**Added in the recording** (not in the kit):
- "confirm international students can work where you're studying before you even try" framing, "please, or you intend to be".
- "Don't just write credits. Understand this course will give me these credits … I have to be in school two times / once every week."
- Elective courses: choose ones where class commitments won't overwhelm you.
- "you have the same one 24 hours" (same calendar tip).
- Meal-prep section is longer ("those four hours … guarantees food for the rest of the week", African food).
- Migraines / hospital and "I believe that God is taking control".
- Fixed-hours jobs: "you can just clock out of work and forget about work … For me, I don't think 5pm is really when work ends."

**Facts to check:**
- 1:02 she says "**At any university** after your first year, you need at least 45 of those [ECTS]". The kit says "At my university" (Tallinn University). It may be whisper mishearing "my" as "any"; if she really said "any", it's too broad (the rule is per school). Worth a listen.
- "In Estonia, full-time study means around 30 ECTS every semester" and "falling into part-time study can result in your permit being revoked": matches the kit's on-screen note (at least 22.5 ECTS per semester, checked every 2 semesters; check your own school).
- Study leave: she says "30 calendar days, 20 of those are paid at your average salary": matches the kit (Adult Education Act; the kit adds "with a letter from your school, for higher education").
- "I've been doing both since October 2025. This month makes it a year": true only if it's posted in October 2026; if it goes out later, the line dates the video.
- "there's no limit to the number of hours" for students working in Estonia: matches the kit.
